target: Se avessi più soldi, comprerei un appartamento.
english: If I had more money, I'd buy an apartment.
tip: Unreal present: 'se' plus the imperfect subjunctive (avessi) with the conditional (comprerei) for a hypothetical.

target: L'ufficio dove lavoro è al terzo piano.
english: The office where I work is on the third floor.
tip: For places, 'dove' can act as the relative 'where/in which': 'l'ufficio dove lavoro'.

target: La sera in cui ci siamo conosciuti pioveva.
english: The evening we met, it was raining.
tip: With time words, 'in cui' means 'when/on which': 'la sera in cui', not 'la sera che'.

target: La storia che mi ha raccontato era commovente.
english: The story he told me was touching.
tip: 'che' serves as both subject and object relative and never changes: 'la storia che mi ha raccontato'.

target: Se tutto va bene, mi laureerò a giugno.
english: If all goes well, I'll graduate in June.
tip: Graduating is reflexive in Italian: 'laurearsi', so 'mi laureerò' = I'll graduate.

target: L'anno prossimo andremo tutti in vacanza in Grecia.
english: Next year we'll all go on vacation to Greece.
tip: Use 'in' with countries and regions: 'in Grecia', 'in Italia'. Cities instead take 'a'.

target: Mi ero svegliato troppo tardi per la riunione.
english: I had woken up too late to make the meeting.
tip: Reflexive verbs take essere, so the past-perfect is mi ero svegliato with ero, and svegliato agrees with the speaker.

target: Quando avrò finito la scuola, cercherò lavoro all'estero.
english: When I've finished school, I'll look for work abroad.
tip: After 'quando' about the future, Italian uses the future perfect: 'quando avrò finito' = when I've finished.

target: Tutto quello che vuole è un po' di tranquillità.
english: All he wants is a little peace and quiet.
tip: 'quello che' (or 'ciò che') means 'what/that which': 'tutto quello che vuole' = all that he wants.

target: Avevo scritto la lettera ma non l'avevo ancora spedita.
english: I had written the letter but hadn't sent it yet.
tip: After a preceding object pronoun the participle agrees: 'l'' stands for la lettera, so 'spedita', feminine.

target: Se avessi saputo che eri malato, sarei venuto a trovarti.
english: If I had known you were sick, I'd have come to visit you.
tip: Past unreal: 'se' plus the pluperfect subjunctive (avessi saputo) with the past conditional (sarei venuto).

target: Avranno già cenato, erano molto affamati quando li ho visti.
english: They must have already had dinner, they were very hungry when I saw them.
tip: The future perfect can express a guess about the past: 'avranno già cenato' = they must have already eaten.

target: Dove saranno finiti i miei occhiali?
english: Where could my glasses have ended up?
tip: In questions the future signals wondering: 'dove saranno finiti?' = where could they have ended up?

target: Rimarrò a casa tutto il fine settimana.
english: I'll stay home the whole weekend.
tip: 'a casa' means 'at home' with no article: 'rimarrò a casa' = I'll stay home.

target: La riunione comincerà alle dieci in punto.
english: The meeting will begin at ten sharp.
tip: 'in punto' after a time means 'sharp/on the dot': 'alle dieci in punto' = at ten sharp.

target: Chi studia con costanza ottiene buoni risultati.
english: Anyone who studies consistently gets good results.
tip: 'Chi' here means 'whoever/anyone who' and always takes a singular verb: 'chi studia... ottiene'.

target: Se continuerà a piovere, il fiume strariperà.
english: If it keeps raining, the river will overflow.
tip: Unlike English, Italian may use the future after 'se' for a real future case: 'se continuerà a piovere'.

target: I colleghi con i quali lavoro sono molto competenti.
english: The colleagues I work with are very competent.
tip: Con i quali is a formal stand-in for con cui, and quali agrees with what it refers to: plural masculine colleghi gives i quali.

target: Sarà stato un malinteso.
english: It must have been a misunderstanding.
tip: Future perfect for past speculation: "Sarà stato difficile" = It must have been hard. Italian uses futuro anteriore to guess about past events.

target: Dopo che avrete mangiato, parleremo.
english: After you've eaten, we'll talk.
tip: After dopo che about the future, Italian uses the future perfect: avrete mangiato (will have eaten), not the present.

target: Quando avrò finito, ti chiamo.
english: When I've finished, I'll call you.
tip: After quando for a finished future action, Italian uses the future perfect avrò finito, while the main clause ti chiamo stays present.

target: Entro domani avrò finito il rapporto.
english: By tomorrow I'll have finished the report.
tip: Entro marks a deadline, meaning by or within a time: entro domani = by tomorrow.

target: Ciò che conta veramente è la salute.
english: What really matters is health.
tip: "Ciò che" – more formal version of 'quello che'.

target: La lettera è stata spedita ieri mattina.
english: The letter was sent yesterday morning.
tip: Passive voice uses essere plus a past participle that agrees with the subject: lettera is feminine, so spedita.

target: Quando chiuderà il museo, avremo visto tutto.
english: When the museum closes, we'll have seen everything.
tip: After quando about the future, Italian uses the future tense chiuderà (closes), where English keeps the present.

target: Quando arriverà l'estate, avrò imparato a nuotare.
english: When summer comes, I'll have learned to swim.
tip: Imparare takes a before an infinitive: imparato a nuotare (learned to swim).

target: Avevano aspettato per ore sotto la pioggia.
english: They had waited for hours in the rain.
tip: Italian says sotto la pioggia (under the rain) where English says in the rain.

target: Era strano che non rispondesse al telefono.
english: It was strange that he wasn't answering the phone.
tip: Era strano che triggers the subjunctive: rispondesse is the imperfect subjunctive of rispondere.

target: Questo lavoro va fatto subito, non domani.
english: This work must be done right away, not tomorrow.
tip: Va fatto is literally goes done, and andare plus a past participle means must be done: questo lavoro va fatto subito.

target: Se solo il treno non fosse in ritardo!
english: If only the train weren't late!
tip: Se solo plus the imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish: fosse (were), from essere.
